en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty The Fourteenth Chapter
Discourse on the Included:
Does lust for the form realm underlie the form realm? Yes. Is it included within the form realm? Yes.

Is it associated with, co-arisen with, conjoined with, and associated with the mind that is to be attained in meditative absorption (samāpattesiya), the mind that is to be attained upon rebirth (upapattesiya), and the mind that dwells in happiness in this very life (diṭṭhadhammasukhavihāra)—
arising together, ceasing together, having the same basis, and having the same object?
It should not be said thus...
[as before] ...Is it not the case that it is neither desirable for attainment, nor desirable for rebirth, nor a pleasant abiding in this very life;
and that it is not accompanied by, nor co-nascent with, a mind that is desirable for attainment, nor a mind that is desirable for rebirth, nor a mind that is a pleasant abiding in this very life?
Is it associated, conjoined, co-arising, co-ceasing, having the same basis, and having the same object? Yes.

If it is not to be attained through meditative absorption, not to be attained at rebirth, and not a pleasant abiding in this very life … [and so on] … having the same object, then indeed, sir, you should not say: [that it is associated, etc., while being such].
“Attachment to form underlies the form element; it is included within the form element. … [etc.
… Does attachment to form underlie the form element, and is it included within the form element? Yes.
Does lust for sound underlie the sound-element, such that it is included within the sound-element?
One should not say so … [and so on] … Does lust for form underlie the form-element, such that it is included within the form-element?
"Yes. "Sensual lust for odors... [and so on] ...sensual lust for tastes... [and so on].
“Lust for the tangible inheres in the tangible element; it is included within the tangible element”?
One should not say so… [and so on]… “Lust for sound inheres in the sound element; one should not say it is included within the sound element”? One should not say so.
“If it is accepted that [desire] is included within the sphere of form, then is it not the case that desire for form underlies the sphere of form?
Yes, it is so.
Therefore, it should not be said that desire for form does not underlie the sphere of form.”
“Is it included within the realm of form (rūpadhātu)?
One should not say so …pe… [and likewise for] craving for odors (gandharāga) …pe…
Taste-attachment …pe… tangible-object-attachment underlies the tangible-object element;
should it not be said that it is included within the tangible-object element?
“Yes.
“Does lust for the form realm underlie the form realm? Should it not be said that it is ‘included within the form realm’?”
It should not be said so … [as before] … Does lust for the formless realm underlie the formless realm, and is it included within the formless realm? Yes.

Is it associated with, co-arisen with, conjoined with, and associated with the mind that is desirable for attainment, the mind that is desirable for rebirth, and the mind that is a pleasant abiding in this very life;
and is it of one arising, one cessation, one basis, and one object?

It should not be stated thus … [as before] … Is it not the case that it is neither to be attained through meditative absorption, nor to be attained through rebirth, nor is it a pleasant dwelling in this very life; and that it is not by a mind to be attained through absorption … [as before] … that it has a single object?
Yes, it is.
If it is not obtainable through attainment, nor obtainable through rebirth … [and so on] … having a single object,
then indeed, sir, you should not say:
“Lust for the formless realm underlies [the mind], and it is included within the formless realm.”
Does attachment to the formless underlie the formless element, and is it included within the formless element?
Yes. Does attachment to sound underlie the sound element, and is it included within the sound element?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Does lust for the formless realm underlie the formless realm, and is it included within the formless realm? Yes.
Is lust for odors... pe...
lust for tastes... pe...
lust for tangibles latent in the tangible element; is it included within the tangible element?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Sound-desire underlies the sound-element;
should it not be said that it is “included within the sound-element”?
“Yes.
“Lust for the formless realm underlies the formless realm;
yet it should not be said that it is ‘included within the formless realm. “It should not be said so,” [you reply]. …pe…
Scent-attachment …pe… taste-attachment …pe… touch-attachment underlies the element of the tangible; it should not be said that—
“Is it included within the tangible element? Yes.
[If so,] then while formless lust underlies the formless element, one should not say—
“Is it included within the formless realm?
One should not say so …pe… It should not be said—
“Is attachment to form latent in the form realm and included within the form realm? Is attachment to the formless latent in the formless realm and included within the formless realm?”—Yes.
[If so,] is it not the case that attachment to sense-pleasures is latent in the sense-sphere realm and is included within the sense-sphere realm?
“Yes.
“If sensual lust underlies the sense-sphere realm and is included within the sense-sphere realm, then indeed it must be said:
‘Form-lust underlies the form-sphere realm and is included within the form-sphere realm; formless-lust underlies the formless-sphere realm and is included within the formless-sphere realm.’”
The Discussion on the Included is finished.
